extracted.intended_audience: design applicants, geographical indication/traditional product applicants, IP practitioners and registrants in Turkey
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and evaluation standards from Turkish intellectual property law covering geographical indications, traditional product names, and industrial/design registration: validity/invalidity, infringement, design novelty/individual character, application/examination, publication/postponement, opposition, and term/renewal. Useful for applicants, attorneys, and examiners handling Turkish IP filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for invalidity of geographical indication or traditional specialty guaranteed
rubrics_metrics.description: Invalidity of a geographical indication or traditional specialty guaranteed may be requested from the court by persons who have interest. The court shall decide the registered geographical indication or traditional specialty guaranteed invalid in case: a) The register is not in compliance with any one of the conditions set out in the Articles 33, 34, 35, 37 or 39; b) The registration has not been made by those who have right to apply in line with the Article 36; c) Controls are not carried out as set out in Article 49.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invalidity proceedings are instituted against the registrant recorded in the register; the Office is not a party to these proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of invalidity for geographical indications and traditional product names
rubrics_metrics.description: If a geographical indication or traditional specialty guaranteed is decided invalid by the court, the legal protection provided by this Code for the registered geographical sign or traditional product name shall be deemed not to have arisen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retroactive effects of invalidity shall not extend to: a) Any final judgments for infringement of registration rights reached and enforced prior to the decision of invalidity; b) Contracts concluded and executed prior to the decision of invalidity. Partial or total reimbursement of sums paid under contracts may be claimed on grounds of equity. Final court decisions are notified to the Office ex officio and the invalidated sign/name is cancelled from the register and published in the Bulletin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of rights and consequences of withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: The registrant may withdraw from the rights provided by the registration and the responsibilities related to inspections. The demand of withdrawal is published in the Bulletin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a request for change of registrant is filed by eligible parties within three months after publication, it is examined per Article 43. If no request is filed within three months, the sign/name is cancelled from the register and published. Withdrawal produces effect from the date of its entry to the register. Procedure and rules related to withdrawal are to be determined by implementing regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts deemed as infringement of a registered geographical sign
rubrics_metrics.description: The following uses of a registered geographical sign shall be considered infringement: a) Any direct or indirect commercial use of the registered geographical sign or emblem in relation to products within the scope of the register or comparable products to exploit the reputation where they do not carry the properties specified in the register; b) Any deceptive use, replicas or associative use about the place of origin or translation of the geographical sign even if accompanied by expressions such as 'style', 'type', 'method', 'as produced in'; c) Any use of false or misleading indication or description about the origin or properties specified in the geographical sign register on packaging, promotional material or any written material related to the product; ç) Any deceptive use of the emblem of registered geographical sign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those who have the right to use the geographical sign may request a claim by notifying the registrant via notary and filing suit if not accepted within three months. In case of serious risk of harm, precautionary rulings may be sought regardless of time limits. Lack of presentation of registration record on product does not exclude infringement but is considered in fault evaluation. Where an application is published, the applicant may appeal to the Court for acts of infringement; if the aggressor was informed of the application and acts in bad faith, infringement may be accepted prior to publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts deemed as infringement of a registered traditional product name
rubrics_metrics.description: The following uses of a registered traditional product name shall be considered infringement: a) Any commercial use of the registered traditional product name together with the emblem to exploit reputation for products which do not carry the properties specified in the register or use of the emblem on resembling products; b) Any deceptive usage of the emblem; c) Any use of misleading indications or descriptions on packaging, promotional and advertising material or any written material related to the product which does not carry the properties specified in the traditional product name register and emblem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforcement procedure mirrors that for geographical signs: right-holders notify registrant through notary; if no response or claim within three months they may file suit; precautionary rulings are available for serious risk of harm; applicants whose application is published may sue for infringements and bad faith by aggressor may render acts infringing prior to publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of design and product
rubrics_metrics.description: Design is the appearance of the whole or part of a product resulting from the features of line, contour, colour, shape, material or texture of the product itself or its ornamentation. Product means any industrial or handicraft item, including parts intended to be assembled into a complex product, packaging, presentations of more than one object perceived together, graphic symbols and typographic typefaces, but excluding computer programs. Complex product is a product composed of components which can be replaced or renewed by disassembly and reassembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A design is protected as a registered design if registered under the Act; non-registered design protection arises if presented to the public for the first time in Turkey.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty and individual character requirements for designs
rubrics_metrics.description: A design shall be protected provided that it is new and has an individual character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A design is new if an identical design has not been presented to the public anywhere before the application/priority date (or before first public presentation for non-registered designs). Designs differing only in immaterial details are identical. A design has individual character if the overall impression on the informed user differs from any design presented to the public before the relevant date. In assessing distinctive character, the degree of freedom of the designer in developing the design shall be taken into consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty/individual character for parts of complex products and 'normal use'
rubrics_metrics.description: The design of a part of a complex product is considered new and to have distinctive character if: a) the component part is mounted and remains visible during normal use of the complex product; b) the visible features of the component part fulfill the requirements as to novelty and individual character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Normal use' means use by the end user, excluding maintenance, servicing or repair work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure (making available to the public) and 12-month grace period
rubrics_metrics.description: Making available to the public includes releasing on the market, use, description, publication, promotion, exhibition and sale; disclosure to a third person under conditions of confidentiality is not making available to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A disclosure shall not affect novelty or individual character if the design was made available to the public during the 12-month period preceding the filing or priority date by the designer, successor in title, a third person with consent of the designer, or by abuse of relation with the designer or successor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of design protection and exclusions from protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Design owner may use rights against designs which have no individual character compared to his own design. In assessing scope, the degree of freedom of the designer in developing his design shall be taken into consideration. Design protection does not prejudice protection under the Intellectual and Artistic Works Act if conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The following shall not be in the scope of protection: a) designs contrary to public policy or morality; b) appearance characteristics dictated by the technical function; c) appearance characteristics that must necessarily be reproduced in exact form and dimensions to allow mechanical connection or incorporation; ç) designs including inappropriate use of sovereignty signs (Article 6ter Paris Convention) or signs affecting public order and religious/historical/cultural values for which registration shall not be granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design rights conferred and limitations/exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: A design confers on its holder the exclusive right to use it; third parties without consent cannot produce, put on the market, sell, import, use for commercial purposes or keep in stock for those purposes the product in which the design is incorporated or to which it is applied, or recommend such contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unregistered design rights allow prevention of use of identical copies or indistinguishably similar overall impression copies. Independent designers who could not reasonably know of prior public presentation are not deemed to have copied. Rights are not exercised for: (a) private non-commercial acts; (b) experimental purposes; (c) reproduction for citation/teaching consistent with fair trade practice and not unduly prejudicing normal exploitation, with source mentioned; (ç) training/reference reproductions in good faith. Additional exceptions: equipment on foreign-registered ships/aircraft temporarily entering Turkey and importation of spare parts for repair; repair of complex product parts restoring original appearance within three years after design release is not infringement provided no misleading source information; use of equivalent parts published by the Ministry within three years is not infringement. For designs with deferred publication, unregistered-design provisions apply until visual representation is published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right arising from previous use
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural persons and legal entities that have used the design in the registered scope of protection independently and in good faith for commercial purposes inside the country, or took serious and true measures for use, shall be given the right to use due to previous use limited to preparations to meet reasonable enterprise requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Right arising from previous use shall be registered and published in the Bulletin, cannot be extended or licensed, and may only be transferred via transfer of the enterprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design application content and form requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A design application shall cover: a) application form with applicant identity; b) the visual representation that reflects the appearance of the design and enables reproduction through publication; c) the name of the product in which the design is incorporated or applied; ç) the name of the designer or group members; d) information on how registration request right has been obtained from the designer; e) if any, request of postponement of publication; f) if engaged, information related to the attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For two-dimensional designs with postponement request, a sample may be given instead of visual representation. Description or sample and product class may be indicated but do not affect scope of protection. Fees must be paid or application is invalid. Locarno classification applies. Written statements of visual representation do not provide exclusive rights to concepts they express. Multiple applications rules, correction of spelling/obvious factual mistakes (without changing sample), and other procedural provisions are set by regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple applications and division rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple design registration can be made as multiple applications if additional fee is paid. In multiple applications, except for ornamentation, each product design used for/fitted to must be of the same class. Multiple applications/designs forming multiple registrations are evaluated separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If designs in a multiple application do not comply with rules or exceed number limits, the Office requests separate applications; for each divided application, application date is that of the first application and priority right is recognized if claimed in first application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority right: eligibility, time limits and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural persons/legal entities (or successors) who are citizens of Paris Convention contracting countries or WTO members, or who have settlement/commercial organization in such countries, may claim priority to make application in Turkey for identical design within six months from the date of their first duly made application to competent authorities; priority rights not used within this period are forfeited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority may also be based on exhibition of the design/product at recognized national/international exhibitions within six months. Documents of priority must be obtained from competent authorities and submitted to the Office within three months of application date or the request is void. If more than one priority is claimed, the earliest date applies. Priority rules are further regulated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of design applications and grounds for refusal
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office examines compliance with Articles 61 and 63. If no deficiency in the required items (application form and visual representation) is found, application date finalizes as of receipt; deficiencies remedied in due time result in date as of remedy; failure to remedy results in invalidation. Design protection begins from the date of finalisation of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office rejects registration requests that: a) do not comply with design/product description; b) violate public policy or morality; c) are made by persons/entities not within scope of Article 3; ç) contain inappropriate use of sovereignty signs (Article 6ter Paris Convention) or signs affecting public order/cultural values; d) are determined not to be new. Partial refusal may be given for only a section; remaining section must meet protection conditions and maintain design identity to ensure continuity of registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration, publication and public access to registry
rubrics_metrics.description: A not-refused finalized application shall be recorded in the registry as a registered design and published in the Bulletin. The registry shall be open to the public and an example of the registration provided upon request and payment of fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures and rules relating to registry recording, publishing process and registration operations are determined by regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postponement of publication: rules, effects and obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may request postponement of publication for a period of thirty months starting from the application date or, if applicable, the priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a postponement request is not rejected, the application is registered but visual representations and application files are not made publicly available until expiry. Demand for postponement is published in the Bulletin. On expiry (or earlier at rights owner's request upon payment of publication fee) the Office shall submit and publish records and documents. If only a sample was given during application, a visual representation suitable for publication must be submitted or protection is invalid from application date. Information in the registry and application file must be notified to the defendant to allow infringement actions during postponement. Publication date for a deferred design is the date of publication of the visual representation. Provisions may apply to some designs in multiple applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition: who may oppose, grounds and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may raise a justified, written objection against decisions under Article 64 within two months of notification. Third parties may object in writing to issuing of registration certificate within three months from the publication date by paying the fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grounds for third-party objections include that the design does not fulfill definitions of Article 55, fails to meet conditions in Articles 56 and 57, is within the exclusion of Article 58(4) or Article 64(6)(ç), application made in bad faith, or contains unauthorized use of intellectual property rights. If objection fee not paid or proof not submitted in time, objection is invalid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of oppositions and possible outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Oppositions are examined by the Board. The applicant's opinion is taken during examination if necessary. Opposing party may be asked to submit additional information/documents within one month. If additional information is not submitted, examination proceeds on existing records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If deficiencies are found during opposition stage, operations continue from the incomplete stage and decisions published. If objection under third-party grounds is accepted, registration is deemed invalid (or partially invalidated for a part). At the end of partial invalidation, remaining part must meet protection conditions and keep design identity. If registration is invalidated, invalidity results specified in Article 79 enter into force and invalidity decision is published in the Bulletin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of protection and renewal for registered designs
rubrics_metrics.description: The term of protection of a registered design covers a period of five years from the date of filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This period may be prolonged up to a total of twenty-five years by renewing in five-year periods.
